hero_subtitle: A lightweight, open-source macOS menu bar app for managing displays and creating virtual monitors.
features_title: Everything you need, nothing you don't
features_desc: Simple display management that lives in your menu bar and stays out of the way.
feat_toggle_desc: Turn monitors off for real: they go dark and leave the desktop, and come back with one click. Prefer to keep one on? Mirror it onto the main display instead. A 15-second countdown protects your last visible screen.
feat_virtual_desc: Create virtual monitors with custom resolutions and device presets — iPhone, iPad, Mac, TV, and more.
feat_main_desc: Change your primary monitor from the menu bar. Menu bar and dock reposition automatically.
feat_hidpi_desc: Pick the resolution and zoom of any display from its row: Retina "looks like" sizes, native sizes and refresh rates. Virtual displays can be Retina and remember the mode you choose.
feat_sleep_desc: Automatically handles display state across sleep cycles. Your setup is restored without manual intervention.
feat_color_desc: Prevents the ColorSync deadlock with identical monitors on macOS Sequoia, and gives virtual displays a stable identity so they don't leak ICC profiles or keep colorsyncd busy.
vd_desc: macOS limits resolution when no physical monitor is connected. SimpleDisplay creates virtual displays that the system treats as real screens — perfect for remote access, testing, and headless setups.
vd_remote_desc: Full resolution over any remote desktop. Works best with Remote Display, our remote desktop for macOS whose virtual monitors resize to your window; also with Screen Sharing, VNC, Parsec, AnyDesk or TeamViewer.
vd_headless_desc: Run Mac minis and Mac Studios with no monitor attached at any resolution.
vd_responsive_desc: Test layouts at specific device resolutions without extra hardware.
vd_hidden_desc: Keep apps running on a virtual display while working on your main screen.
how_desc: SimpleDisplay uses macOS private frameworks to give you control that the built-in settings don't offer.
how_virtual_desc: Uses Apple's private CGVirtualDisplay API to create displays that appear as real monitors to macOS — useful for screen sharing specific resolutions, testing responsive layouts, or keeping apps running on a "hidden" screen.
how_disable_desc: Deactivates it at the window-server level via CGSConfigureDisplayEnabled, the same private API displayplacer uses. The display goes dark and leaves the desktop while staying connected; SimpleDisplay keeps a greyed-out row so you can turn it back on.
how_why_desc: These capabilities aren't available through public frameworks. SimpleDisplay can't be distributed on the Mac App Store, but it can do things no App Store app can.
auto_desc: Every action is also a simpledisplay:// URL, and the simpledisplayctl command wraps them for shell scripts, Shortcuts, launchd agents, or an SSH session into a Mac with no monitor attached. The URL launches the app if it isn't running, so there is no extra background process.
auto_cli_desc: Create, resize and remove virtual displays, and turn any display off, on or into a mirror, by name or ID with simpledisplayctl. Install it from a checkout with make cli-install.
auto_url_desc: open, create, remove, reconfigure, enable, disable (with an optional headless confirmation), mirror, unmirror, mode and status. Every value is validated before the app acts on it, and malformed URLs show a one-line banner instead of failing silently.
auto_ssh_desc: Run the CLI over SSH to drive the SimpleDisplay running on that Mac, for example to set a resolution before connecting with Remote Display or Screen Sharing.
start_desc: Download the DMG or build from source — your choice.
start_download_desc: Grab the latest DMG from GitHub Releases. Open it, drag to Applications, and you're done.
start_first_launch_desc: Since v1.6.1 the app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any other app. Older builds were blocked on first launch: go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, once.
start_build_desc: Clone the repo and build with a single command. Requires Xcode Command Line Tools.
lim_desc: SimpleDisplay uses private Apple APIs. Here's what that means in practice.
lim_1: Cannot be distributed on the Mac App Store — private APIs are not allowed by Apple's review guidelines.
lim_2: Virtual display refresh rate is supported up to 240 Hz (the old 60 Hz cap was an app-side limit, not an API one).
lim_3: Enable/disable and main-display state are tracked by a stable per-display UUID, but the identical-monitor ColorSync fix and simpledisplayctl remove --name match displays by name, so two monitors with the same name may not be distinguishable there.
lim_4: The CGVirtualDisplay and CGSConfigureDisplayEnabled APIs are undocumented and may change or be removed in future macOS versions.
lim_5: Virtual displays can't be mirror sources: on macOS 26 that crashes the window server, so SimpleDisplay refuses it. Mirror a physical display onto a virtual one instead.
community_desc: SimpleDisplay is free software. Built with insights from the macOS display management community, including BetterDisplay, DeskPad, and displayplacer. Contributions of all kinds are welcome.
